extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting short science fiction and fantasy stories to Clarkesworld Magazine
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting short science fiction and fantasy stories to Clarkesworld Magazine, covering length, format, rights, pay, content preferences and anti-patterns, and the online submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word Limit
rubrics_metrics.description: 1000-8000 words (preferred length is 4000)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred length of 4000; adhere to minimum 1000 and maximum 8000 unless otherwise indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: 10¢ per word for the first 4000 words, 6¢ for each word over 4000
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment is per word with a tiered rate; ensure word count is accurate on submission form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres Accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Science fiction and fantasy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science fiction need not be 'hard' SF, but rigor is appreciated. Fantasy can be folkloric, medieval, contemporary, surreal, etc. Horror can be supernatural or psychological, so long as it is frightening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language
rubrics_metrics.description: English
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must be in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights Claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: We claim first world electronic rights (text and audio), first print rights (author must be willing to sign 100+ chapbooks), and non-exclusive anthology rights for our annual Clarkesworld anthology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be prepared to sign required print chapbook agreements and understand electronic/anthology rights claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Quality of Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories must be: Well-written. Language is important. There is no distinction between 'style' and 'substance' or 'story' and 'writing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize strong craft and language; poor writing will hurt a story regardless of concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-screen Readability / Formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Convenient for on-screen reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very long paragraphs or typographical trickery may work against you. Use a layout and formatting suitable for reading on screens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Profanity/Gore/Sexuality
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no barriers as to levels of profanity, gore, or sexuality allowed, but high amounts of profanity, gore, and sexuality are generally used poorly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you include extreme content, ensure it is well-used and serves the story rather than relying on shock value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science Fiction Rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Science fiction need not be 'hard' SF, but rigor is appreciated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if not 'hard' SF, internal consistency and thoughtful treatment of speculative elements strengthen a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horror Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Horror can be supernatural or psychological, so long as it is frightening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primary requirement is that the story is genuinely frightening in its approach, whether via supernatural or psychological means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milquetoast Civilian Government Trope (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: stories in which a milquetoast civilian government is depicted as the sole obstacle to either catching some depraved criminal or to an uncomplicated military victory
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This scenario is listed as a likely hard sell; avoid relying on an impotent civilian government as a primary plot obstacle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'thou' or 'thine' (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: stories in which the words "thou" or "thine" appear
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid archaic second-person pronouns unless absolutely justified and skillfully handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talking Cats (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: talking cats
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The trope of talking cats is called out as a hard sell; consider originality and avoidance of clichéd anthropomorphic pets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talking Swords (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: talking swords
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Talking weapon tropes are discouraged as they tend to be overused or gimmicky.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climax Dependent on Spilling of Intestines (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: stories where the climax is dependent on the spilling of intestines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid gore-dependent climaxes that rely on visceral splatter as the primary emotional or plot payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: TV-style Easy FTL (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: stories where FTL travel is as easy as is it on television shows or movies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portrayals of faster-than-light travel that treat it as a trivial convenience are unlikely to impress; more thoughtful handling preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Travel (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: time travel too
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time travel stories are listed as hard sells—ensure originality and rigorous handling if you choose this trope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on Vestigial Judeo-Christian Mythology (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: stories that depend on some vestigial belief in Judeo-Christian mythology in order to be frightening (i.e., Cain and Abel are vampires, the End Times are a' comin', Communion wine turns to Christ's literal blood and it's HIV positive, Satan's gonna getcha, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid simplistic uses of Judeo-Christian motifs as a cheap source of fright; be more inventive or substantive in religious/mythic treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapist-Murderer-Cannibals (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: stories about rapist-murderer-cannibals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extremely violent/sexually violent cannibalistic plotlines are flagged as hard sells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children Discover Anything Trope (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: stories about young kids playing in some field and discovering ANYTHING. (a body, an alien craft, Excalibur, ANYTHING).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the cliché of children casually stumbling on a major plot device; it's overused and unlikely to stand out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehashed Popular-Science Content (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: stories about the stuff we all read in Scientific American three months ago
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid thinly fictionalized versions of recent popular-science articles; strive for original speculative leaps rather than topical riffing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party Takeover/Partisan Utopia/Dystopia (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: stories where the Republicans, or Democrats, or Libertarians, or the Spartacist League, etc. take over the world and either save or ruin it
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overtly partisan 'party takes over world' plots are poor sells; nuanced political fiction is better received than caricatured takeover scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Your AD&D Game (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: your AD&D game
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that read like a recounting of a tabletop campaign (AD&D-style) are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pun-dependent Humor (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: "funny" stories that depend on, or even include, puns
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor that relies primarily on puns is unlikely to be well-received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexy Vampires/Werewolves/Pirates (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: sexy vampires, wanton werewolves, or lusty pirates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Romanticized/sexified monsters and lusty pirate tropes are flagged as common and unwelcome unless done in a fresh way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zombies or Zombie-wannabes (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: zombies or zombie-wannabes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zombie stories and imitations are considered poor sells due to market saturation and trope fatigue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stories Written for Upcoming Theme Anthology (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: stories originally intended for someone's upcoming theme anthology or issue
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit work that was specifically written for a themed anthology or issue elsewhere—these are hard sells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protagonist Admired/Despised Solely for Being Smart/Strange (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: stories where the protagonist is either widely despised or widely admired simply because he or she is just so smart and/or strange
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid characters who are treated as exceptional or ostracized solely as a one-note trait (smart/strange) without deeper characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inauthentic Artsy-fartsy Bohemia Setting (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: stories that take place within an artsy-fartsy bohemia as written by an author who has clearly never experienced one
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid shallow, stereotyped depictions of bohemian subcultures; authenticity matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trunk Stories (Hard Sell)
rubrics_metrics.description: your trunk stories
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Old, unpolished 'trunk' stories that authors keep revisiting are likely hard sells unless substantially reworked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Method
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarkesworld uses an online submissions system that has been designed to streamline our process and improve communication with authors. We do not accept email or paper submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit only via the specified online submissions form; email and paper submissions will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Form Fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Our submissions form asks for your name, email address, cover letter, story title, word count, genre and story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all required fields are completed accurately when submitting via the online form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Letter Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Your cover letter should contain your publishing history (if any) and any other relevant information (e.g, if you send us a lusty pirate story and happen to BE a lusty pirate, mention that).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concise publishing history and any relevant contextual details that might affect acceptance or rights; be professional and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted File Formats
rubrics_metrics.description: All stories should be in standard manuscript format and can be submitted in either .RTF or .DOC format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard manuscript formatting and submit only .RTF or .DOC files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript Format
rubrics_metrics.description: All stories should be in standard manuscript format
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow standard manuscript conventions (e.g., readable font, double-spaced or standard conventions) suitable for professional submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous Submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: No simultaneous submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit the same story to multiple markets while it is under consideration here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Confirmation / Tracking Number
rubrics_metrics.description: After you have submitted your story, a tracking number will be displayed and an automated email confirmation containing this information will be sent to you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have not received the confirmation email within 24 hours, email the editor. Keep your tracking number to monitor submission status and check your spam folder (Yahoo.com may treat emails as spam).

rubrics_metrics.name: Response Time and Query Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our average response time is under two days, but we occasionally hold submissions for longer periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send queries until after two weeks have passed. Use your tracking number to check status prior to that.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't send revisions to a submission unless they have been requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only submit revised versions when specifically requested by the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiting Period After Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't submit another story for a period of seven days after receiving a rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect the seven-day waiting period before sending a different story after a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do Not Resubmit Rejected Stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't re-submit stories that have been rejected. Do not query for permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send the same rejected story again or ask for permission to resubmit; move on to new material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't argue with rejection slips. You're only wasting time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept editorial decisions gracefully; arguing about rejections is discouraged and counterproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: When in Doubt, Be Conservative
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are uncertain about anything above, we recommend following the most conservative interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When unsure about policies or what to submit, default to the stricter reading of these guidelines.
